item.text: {"question_id":"4B.6","answer":"In 2023, the ruler-period record shows limited formal openness but materially constrained independent information in practice. The April 2023 press-law revision guaranteed access to non-classified information of public interest and followed consultations, but tightened journalist-access requirements, retained possible prison sentences for press offenses, and added a bad-faith false-information clause; the supplied evidence does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal authorship or how the law was judicially enforced. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0011-E011] Authorities did not restrict or disrupt internet access or censor online content in 2023, and the CENI announced a mixed national-international external audit of the voter register with conflict-of-interest rules and planned publication of results. [BATCH-0011-E011, BATCH-0027-E011] The DRC initially invited a nationwide EU observation mission, although it was later reduced to an eight-person expert mission based in Kinshasa; the supplied EEAS record does not explain the reduction, while HRW reports that authorities did not authorize satellite equipment. [BATCH-0028-E007, BATCH-0028-E003, BATCH-0002-E018] Against these qualifying points, RSF described a state broadcaster lacking independence, political and local-authority pressure, precarious and politically influenced media ownership and funding, common self-censorship, and 2023 risks including arrests, threats, attacks, disappearances, and impunity. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0025-E008] The 2023 country report recorded arbitrary arrests and intimidation of journalists, pressure by provincial authorities, criminal defamation and false-information provisions, and increased self-censorship after Stanis Bujakera’s September arrest and pretrial detention; it also recorded a June beating and detention of three journalists by FARDC soldiers, with no supplied evidence of disciplinary accountability. [BATCH-0011-E011, BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E007] During the December election period, UDPS supporters attacked journalist Pascal Mulegwa, AREP supporters attacked Réné Mobembo, and CSAC ordered Perfect Télévision off air after reports about polling irregularities; the station remained off air as of December 22. [BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003] OLPA separately warned in November that provincial media regulation was nearly nonexistent, with under-equipped, under-resourced, and disorganized CSAC offices creating conditions conducive to disinformation and ethnic or tribal hate speech. [BATCH-0006-E009] Tshisekedi claimed a 30-place improvement in the RSF barometer over four years, but that presidential claim is not independently substantiated by the supplied record. [BATCH-0022-E006] The evidence therefore supports some formal and procedural openness, including no recorded nationwide internet censorship, but not a reliably independent information system. The incidents and laws cited are principally 2023 evidence; broader RSF descriptions concern the 2023 country assessment, while the Bujakera case and other campaign incidents should not be read as a complete five-year total. Personal presidential direction of individual abuses is generally not established, so attribution is primarily to state authorities, regulators, security forces, or party supporters rather than to Tshisekedi personally.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0006-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0002-E018","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0022-E006","BATCH-0027-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied record does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal authorship, order, or endorsement of most restrictions or abuses.","The press-law text’s judicial interpretation, implementation, and final enforcement outcomes are not supplied.","The record does not establish whether the CENI audit was completed, published, or acted upon.","The reason for the EU mission reduction and the mission’s eventual findings are unresolved.","Media ownership, funding, licensing practice, and remedies for journalist attacks are incompletely documented.","Evidence involving non-state actors, provincial authorities, security forces, and party supporters cannot automatically be attributed to the president.","The presidential RSF-improvement claim lacks independent supporting scores in the supplied evidence. "],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported specific RSF ranking cited in the draft.","Restored and integrated the qualifying evidence on absent nationwide internet restriction, CENI’s external-audit procedures, the initial EU invitation, and Tshisekedi’s self-reported RSF improvement claim.","Corrected the period framing by distinguishing direct 2023 incidents and legislation from broader 2023 country-assessment context and avoiding an unsupported five-year journalist-arrest total.","Preserved the attribution limits for Tshisekedi, state authorities, regulators, security forces, and party supporters.","Retained the material adverse evidence on provincial regulatory weakness, Bujakera, FARDC abuse, election-period attacks, and the Perfect Télévision shutdown."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller ledger review would be warranted if additional evidence can establish presidential control, knowledge, corrective action, or accountability for CSAC, security-force, broadcaster, or journalist cases.","Additional independent evidence on media ownership, licensing, funding transparency, judicial enforcement, and the completed CENI and EU processes could materially refine the assessment."]}
